summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Morning in the operations bullpen. Every terminal refreshes at once with a corporate review banner while ordinary work continues around it. Middle image: Astra freezes mid-coffee while still holding a stack of normal work orders. Closing image: Jax looks from his cart to the growing stack of category stickers.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Morning in the operations bullpen. Every terminal refreshes at once with a corporate review banner while ordinary work continues around it.
PANEL 2 — Pixa lights up beside a cart Jax is trying to move through the room.
PANEL 3 — Astra freezes mid-coffee while still holding a stack of normal work orders.
PANEL 4 — Glorp scrolls through the new classification tree as a label printer begins producing unnecessary category stickers beside him.
PANEL 5 — Jax looks from his cart to the growing stack of category stickers.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Maintenance Bay. Opening image: In the maintenance bay, Zib has the coolant-balancing unit open for its routine temporary-repair check; the replacement-part tag is clipped directly to the housing. Middle image: The physical replacement-part tag and its eighteen-day ETA sit in the same frame as the expedited-procurement eligibility. Closing image: Zib sees the look immediately without looking up from the repair.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — In the maintenance bay, Zib has the coolant-balancing unit open for its routine temporary-repair check; the replacement-part tag is clipped directly to the housing.
PANEL 2 — Mira joins Astra at the open unit while Pixa displays the new station classification on a compact handheld projection.
PANEL 3 — Pixa opens the pilot-benefits section while Zib continues inspecting the approved clamp.
PANEL 4 — The physical replacement-part tag and its eighteen-day ETA sit in the same frame as the expedited-procurement eligibility.
PANEL 5 — Astra looks from the tag to Zib.
PANEL 6 — Zib sees the look immediately without looking up from the repair.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIXA
dialogueInline.text: Pilot sites receive expedited procurement eligibility.

dialogueInline.speaker: ZIB
dialogueInline.text: Don't look at me like that.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Astra returns from the maintenance bay with the eighteen-day replacement-part ETA still open on her slate just as delivery drones arrive with passive-recovery containers. Middle image: Pixa explains that accepting the limited pilot opens an expedited procurement review, not a guaranteed shipment. Closing image: Astra authorizes the pilot only after writing a local boundary across the top of the acceptance screen.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra returns from the maintenance bay with the eighteen-day replacement-part ETA still open on her slate as delivery drones arrive with passive-recovery containers.
PANEL 2 — Jax looks from the containers to Astra's maintenance slate.
PANEL 3 — Pixa displays the actual benefit: expedited procurement review becomes available to active pilot sites; no shipment or outcome is guaranteed.
PANEL 4 — Glorp opens the acceptance screen. Zib does not touch the containers.
PANEL 5 — Astra writes a local condition before signing: PASSIVE COLLECTION DURING NORMAL WORK ONLY.
PANEL 6 — Astra accepts the limited pilot. The containers are now their problem because she chose them.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIXA
dialogueInline.text: Pilot participation opens expedited procurement review.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: No. But eighteen days is eighteen days.

dialogueInline.speaker: GLORP
dialogueInline.text: The acceptance has optional implementation fields.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: Then the first thing we implement is a boundary.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Lab Work Area. Opening image: Astra brings Mira the pilot packet and plainly tells her why she accepted it: the station needs the replacement-part queue reviewed. Middle image: Mira separates defensible physical measurements from the requested staff-condition fields. Closing image: Astra accepts Mira's scientific boundary even though it may weaken the pilot case she just opened.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra puts the pilot packet beside Mira's retained physical samples.
PANEL 2 — Astra shows the eighteen-day replacement-part ETA and the newly opened procurement-review eligibility on the same slate.
PANEL 3 — Mira reads the requested variables and physically covers STAFF CONDITION with one hand.
PANEL 4 — She circles sample mass, cohesion, temperature, location and equipment load.
PANEL 5 — Astra asks whether that narrower dataset is enough to participate honestly.
PANEL 6 — Mira says yes to the material study and no to interpreting coworkers. Astra accepts both answers.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: I accepted it for the procurement review.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: Good. Then we can be honest about the temptation.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: These are measurements. This is speculation.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: Can we give them the first without the second?

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: It may be less useful to them.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: It has to stay useful to us.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Jax is unloading a container when Pixa assigns him the suggested resource-communication role. Middle image: Instead of treating it as symbolic staffing, Jax identifies the bounded operational pieces: container placement, custody, route access and pickup records. Closing image: He accepts because it is a real job with edges.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Jax is unloading a container when Pixa posts RESOURCE COMMUNICATION LIAISON — SUGGESTED: JAX ORIEN.
PANEL 2 — Jax asks for duties instead of reacting to the title.
PANEL 3 — Pixa lists container placement, custody seals, access checks, pickup timing and sample transfer.
PANEL 4 — Jax looks at Astra.
PANEL 5 — Astra gives him the authority to move any collection hardware that interferes with actual work.
PANEL 6 — Jax takes the route slate and leaves Glorp holding the ceremonial job description.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: And if a bin blocks work, the bin loses.

dialogueInline.speaker: GLORP
dialogueInline.text: There is also a role charter.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Jax and Zib walk the station map together, choosing collection locations around access needs instead of around projected yield. Middle image: Mira adds the minimum physical metadata each location can support. Closing image: Jax rejects the highest-traffic placement because it would narrow a service aisle.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Jax and Zib stand over a station map with the new containers still stacked on a cart.
PANEL 2 — Pixa highlights three high-traffic suggested collection points.
PANEL 3 — Zib overlays service clearances and two of the suggestions turn red.
PANEL 4 — Mira adds only physical logging requirements to the remaining locations.
PANEL 5 — Jax moves the highest-traffic bin marker away from a service aisle.
PANEL 6 — Pixa records lower projected collection coverage and unobstructed access.

dialogueInline.speaker: ZIB
dialogueInline.text: Highest projected swearing is also there.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: Location, time, temperature, equipment load, mass.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: The limited pilot starts quietly: most containers are empty and ordinary work continues around them. Middle image: Jax catches Glorp about to add a requested behavioral-context field to the custody sheet and redirects the log to observable conditions only. Closing image: Astra notices Jax enforcing the boundary without asking her first.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The pilot begins with almost nothing happening: empty containers, normal traffic, normal work.
PANEL 2 — Jax checks seals and route clearance rather than watching coworkers.
PANEL 3 — Glorp adds a requested CONTEXT field to the local custody sheet.
PANEL 4 — Jax asks what observable event belongs in it.
PANEL 5 — Glorp changes the field to EQUIPMENT / LOCATION CONTEXT.
PANEL 6 — Astra sees the corrected sheet as she passes and keeps walking.

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Midday, the first pilot status update arrives with almost no material collected. Middle image: The procurement-review line remains tantalizingly open but marked PENDING SUFFICIENT BASELINE. Closing image: Brick recognizes the leverage before Astra says anything.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — A small private pilot status card appears at Astra's terminal; the room itself has no public dashboard.
PANEL 2 — Physical collection totals are low and unremarkable.
PANEL 3 — A separate line reads EXPEDITED PROCUREMENT REVIEW — PENDING SUFFICIENT BASELINE.
PANEL 4 — Mira looks at Astra, then at the eighteen-day part ETA still pinned beside the status card.
PANEL 5 — Brick, passing behind them with coffee, catches the same juxtaposition.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIXA
dialogueInline.text: Current sample volume is below review threshold.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: That used to be good news.

dialogueInline.speaker: BRICK
dialogueInline.text: Just not to the people selling umbrellas.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: The pilot software suggests relocating one bin to a busier junction to improve baseline coverage. Middle image: Jax checks the proposed spot and finds it conflicts with maintenance access. Closing image: Astra chooses the slower dataset rather than sacrificing the access rule she gave Jax.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Pixa proposes a higher-traffic collection location.
PANEL 2 — Jax walks the suggested spot with the route slate.
PANEL 3 — Zib opens the nearby service panel and the suggested bin footprint overlaps the working clearance.
PANEL 4 — Pixa notes that leaving the bin where it is may delay baseline sufficiency.
PANEL 5 — Jax waits for Astra because this choice touches the procurement review.
PANEL 6 — Astra tells him to leave the bin where it does not block the station.

dialogueInline.speaker: ZIB
dialogueInline.text: It may also improve my ability to kick it.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Lab Work Area. Opening image: Mira reviews the thin first-day sample set. Middle image: She finds no pattern and refuses to turn scarcity into a promising result. Closing image: Astra leaves the lab knowing the honest pilot may not help the procurement problem quickly.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Mira lays out the small first-day sample set.
PANEL 2 — The samples vary in cohesion and location with no meaningful pattern.
PANEL 3 — Pixa offers the corporate status label PROMISING EARLY INDICATOR.
PANEL 4 — Mira deletes the adjective and leaves EARLY DATA — INSUFFICIENT.
PANEL 5 — Astra looks at the replacement-part ETA on her slate.
PANEL 6 — Mira closes the sample case instead of producing a better story.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: Low mass. Mixed cohesion. No pattern.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Astra finds Jax updating the empty-bin route instead of trying to increase collection. Middle image: She asks the question she has been avoiding: whether there is any honest way to make the pilot move faster. Closing image: Jax gives her the operational answer rather than the institutional one.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Jax updates route times beside mostly empty collection bins.
PANEL 2 — Astra stops beside him with the pending procurement-review line open.
PANEL 3 — She asks whether any normal work route would legitimately produce more useful collection opportunities.
PANEL 4 — Jax thinks about the actual schedule, not the pilot.
PANEL 5 — He points to ordinary maintenance work due later that day.
PANEL 6 — Brick hears the answer from the next desk and quietly removes one of his conspiracy notes from the board.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: Is there an honest way to make this faster?

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: I knew I promoted you for a reason.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Maintenance Bay. Opening image: An ordinary air-return damper fault sends Zib, Jax and Mira into real work with Astra trailing. Middle image: A small amount of residue appears near a warm cable seam while the repair is active. Closing image: Jax leaves the sample alone until Zib declares the equipment work complete.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — An ordinary station alert reports AIR RETURN DAMPER RESPONSE LAG.
PANEL 2 — Zib is moving before the pilot software can react.
PANEL 3 — Jax brings the route slate and access kit; Mira brings the diagnostic sensor.
PANEL 4 — During the repair, a small amount of residue appears along a warm cable seam.
PANEL 5 — Jax notices it and deliberately keeps working on the access task instead of interrupting Zib.
PANEL 6 — Only after Zib closes the repair does Jax open the custody kit.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Lab Work Area. Opening image: Jax transfers the post-repair sample through the custody process he now owns. Middle image: Mira finds that this sample survives compression better than the earlier passive dust, but cannot say why. Closing image: Pixa marks the pilot baseline sufficient for review without adding a behavioral explanation.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Jax hands Mira the sealed sample with location, equipment load, temperature and time logged.
PANEL 2 — Mira repeats the same physical tests used on prior samples.
PANEL 3 — The sample survives compression better than the thin earlier material.
PANEL 4 — Astra asks the tempting question.
PANEL 5 — Mira refuses causation she cannot support.
PANEL 6 — Pixa updates the status: BASELINE SUFFICIENT FOR REVIEW / MECHANISM UNDETERMINED.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: Can we say why this one held?

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: The procurement-review status finally changes from unavailable to ELIGIBLE FOR EXPEDITED REVIEW; beside it, the eighteen-day replacement-part ETA remains unchanged. Middle image: Astra gets exactly enough institutional reward to make the next request dangerous. Closing image: Mira sees that Astra is relieved anyway.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra's terminal shows EXPEDITED PROCUREMENT REVIEW — ELIGIBLE.
PANEL 2 — The replacement-part ETA beside it still reads 18 DAYS.
PANEL 3 — Pixa explains that eligibility permits review but guarantees nothing.
PANEL 4 — Astra exhales despite herself.
PANEL 5 — Mira notices that the pilot has already bought emotional leverage without buying a part.
PANEL 6 — A new recommendation notification appears before either of them speaks again.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: They gave you a door, not a part.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: Doors are how you get to parts.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: That is exactly why this is dangerous.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: The new recommendation expands the pilot from passive collection into structured collaboration, wellness baseline and scheduled team activity. Middle image: Pixa shows that declining the enhancements may reduce future pilot eligibility. Closing image: Jax recognizes the change immediately: the station is being asked to alter people to support the resource case.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The recommendation opens under the newly eligible procurement review.
PANEL 2 — Suggested pathways list structured collaboration windows, wellness baseline and scheduled team activity blocks.
PANEL 3 — Mira marks them as behavioral interventions rather than material observation.
PANEL 4 — Kreeb reads the participation language closely.
PANEL 5 — Pixa shows the consequence line: declining enhancements may reduce pilot eligibility.
PANEL 6 — Jax looks from that line to the custody log he has been doing successfully.

dialogueInline.speaker: KREEB
dialogueInline.text: That changes the workplace to improve the study.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Astra does not call a philosophical meeting; she asks each person what part of the current pilot is real work and what part would distort it. Middle image: Their answers divide cleanly around the same line. Closing image: Jax's completed custody log becomes the concrete example of what they can keep.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra stands at the real work board with the enhancement request open beside it.
PANEL 2 — Zib points to service access and normal maintenance.
PANEL 3 — Mira points to defensible physical measurements.
PANEL 4 — Kreeb points to the proposed behavior programs.
PANEL 5 — Glorp identifies passive chain of custody as fully supportable.
PANEL 6 — Jax sets down his completed custody log; unlike the enhancement request, it describes work that actually happened.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: What can we keep without changing the station to feed the study?

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: And I can actually do that job.

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Astra submits a narrower pilot: passive material collection continues, behavioral enhancement does not. Middle image: The expedited procurement review remains merely eligible rather than promised. Closing image: Astra sends the refusal anyway.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra completes the pilot response beside the still-unchanged part ETA.
PANEL 2 — PASSIVE MATERIAL COLLECTION: APPROVED.
PANEL 3 — BEHAVIORAL ENHANCEMENT: NOT APPROVED.
PANEL 4 — Pixa warns that future pilot eligibility may be affected.
PANEL 5 — Glorp starts to soften the refusal. Astra stops him and sends it.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Corporate acknowledgement arrives. Middle image: Pixa opens the attached corporate program. Closing image: Glorp finds the policy source.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Corporate acknowledgement arrives.
PANEL 2 — A second line makes pilot eligibility conditional.
PANEL 3 — Astra leans toward the screen.
PANEL 4 — Pixa opens the attached corporate program.
PANEL 5 — Mira reads the description.
PANEL 6 — Glorp finds the policy source.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: That is a behavioral intervention with better branding.

dialogueInline.speaker: GLORP
dialogueInline.text: It is company-wide wellness policy. Declining it is a different form.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Astra and Mira remain at the terminal after everyone else moves on. Middle image: Astra considers that. Closing image: Astra gives her a look.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra and Mira remain at the terminal after everyone else moves on.
PANEL 2 — Astra points at the mandatory baseline notice.
PANEL 3 — Mira points back at the accepted boundary.
PANEL 4 — Astra considers that.
PANEL 5 — Mira continues.
PANEL 6 — Astra gives her a look.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: They did not get the intervention they asked for.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: A week we can measure without pretending it proves anything.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: You make bad news sound peer reviewed.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Jax uploads the passive sample custody report. Middle image: Pixa answers literally. Closing image: Glorp looks over immediately.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Jax uploads the passive sample custody report.
PANEL 2 — Pixa confirms it.
PANEL 3 — Jax scrolls through the finished form.
PANEL 4 — Pixa answers literally.
PANEL 5 — Jax closes the file.
PANEL 6 — Glorp looks over immediately.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIXA
dialogueInline.text: None required by the local boundary.

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: I like this job better now.

dialogueInline.speaker: GLORP
dialogueInline.text: Do not say that near staffing.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Zib relocates the collection bins to a proper rack that does not obstruct service access. Middle image: The two labels overlap badly. Closing image: Glorp and Kreeb reluctantly combine the rules into one readable card while Mira watches. Pixa emits a notification tone.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Zib relocates the collection bins to a proper rack that does not obstruct service access.
PANEL 2 — Kreeb adds a simple label.
PANEL 3 — Glorp adds a second access label.
PANEL 4 — The two labels overlap badly.
PANEL 5 — Astra sees them.
PANEL 6 — Glorp and Kreeb reluctantly combine the rules into one readable card while Mira watches. Pixa emits a notification tone.

dialogueInline.speaker: SIGN
dialogueInline.text: DO NOT MOVE WITHOUT ACCESS CHECK.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: That may be our best data control.

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: A cheerful corporate banner automatically unrolls across the bullpen. Middle image: Zib studies the mounting points. Closing image: Zib keeps looking at it.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — A cheerful corporate banner automatically unrolls across the bullpen.
PANEL 2 — Everyone looks up at it.
PANEL 3 — Zib studies the mounting points.
PANEL 4 — Pixa checks its placement.
PANEL 5 — Zib keeps looking at it.
